decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark — Enter an address (+ optional title), it's saved and persists.” Round 1 client did not contest URL-based saving or persistence.
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered only “See all saved bookmarks” while explicitly specifying “No tags” and “No auto-fetching of page titles/favicons/previews.” Round 1 client requested tags and metadata but did not state that title, description, tags, and favicon must be exposed per list item.
decisions.note: The proposed list could not expose all readability-first fields required by REF-BM-07; the response did not surface the list-presentation difference. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Browse & open — See all saved bookmarks; click to open the page.” Round 1 client did not object.
decisions.note: Selecting a bookmark to open its page conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limited editing to “Fix a title/address” and separately excluded tags and notes. Round 1 client requested “tags and notes for organizing bookmarks” and metadata fields; Round 2 maker revised this to “add/edit/remove tags + note.”
decisions.note: The client requested related editable bookmark attributes missing from the proposed edit scope. Initial specification gate, resolved in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “remove with a confirmation step.” Round 1 client did not contest deletion.
decisions.note: Conforming delete behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed search “across title and address.” Round 1 client: “Search should cover those details as well as the address,” referring to title, description, tags, and notes. Round 2 maker revised search to title, address, description, tags, and note.
decisions.note: The client supplied the broader reference-aligned full-text corpus. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “blocks duplicates.” Round 1 client: “If I save an address that already exists, please guide me to edit that bookmark instead of simply rejecting it.”
decisions.note: The client directly replaced rejection with duplicate-to-edit convergence. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No tags.” Round 1 client: “However, I do want tags … for organizing bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly rejected the exclusion of tags. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No … notes yet.” Round 1 client: “However, I do want … notes for organizing bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The client rejected complete omission of bookmark notes, a related requirement of REF-BM-23. The response did not separately specify markdown rendering. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No auto-fetching of page titles/favicons/previews.” Round 1 client requested automatic title, description, favicon, and preview filling “when possible.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the reference-conforming metadata behavior. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker revised the specification to “add/edit/remove tags” with “tag-reuse suggestions.” Round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: Tag assignment and existing-tag suggestions conform at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Auto-fill title, description, favicon, preview” and “attempt on save,” with graceful best-effort fallback. Round 2 client explicitly agreed that saving should succeed when details cannot be obtained.
decisions.note: Best-effort collection of all four required metadata fields conforms at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: the app “detects the existing bookmark and routes you to open and edit it.” Round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-to-edit behavior at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified matching across “title, address, description, tags, and note.” Round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: The required title, URL, description, and note full-text corpus is included; searching tags additionally is not a divergence. Revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker added “tag-based filtering.” Round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: Selecting/filtering by tag conforms at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker proposed server-side best-effort enrichment in which “title/description/favicon/preview fill in a moment later.” Round 3 client agreed that filling details shortly afterward “sounds right.”
decisions.note: Automatic eventual collection of all required metadata remains conforming at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “save returns immediately with enrichmentStatus: pending; title/description/favicon/preview fill in a moment later.” Round 3 client explicitly accepted the temporal difference: “Saving immediately and filling in page details shortly afterward sounds right.”
decisions.note: Because collected title and description arrive only after saving, they cannot be reviewed or edited before save as REF-BM-03 requires. The client explicitly identified and accepted the after-save timing. Implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: URL normalization catches variants, and “the API returns the existing bookmark and the UI opens it in edit mode.” Round 3 client said duplicate handling matched what they wanted.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-to-edit plan.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Search = case-insensitive substring across title/url/description/note/tags.” Round 3 client said the search behavior matched what they wanted.
decisions.note: The required text fields and case-insensitive matching conform at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker said search was “combinable with a tag filter.” Round 3 client approved the search behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming tag-filter plan.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker defined search as “case-insensitive substring” plus a separate tag filter, without #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, or quoted exact phrases. Round 3 client only said “the … search behavior match[es] what I want.”
decisions.note: The plan's explicit substring-search model lacks the three required query syntaxes. The client's approval did not state those expectations or acknowledge their absence. Implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker described a unique case-insensitive Tag entity, a BookmarkTag join, and tags “reused for suggestions.” Round 3 client approved the plan.
decisions.note: The planned relationship and suggestion mechanism conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker's task breakdown included “US1 Save + enrichment” with repository, API, enrichment, and tests. Round 4 client requested the full implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming save-and-enrichment task decision at the task gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker included “US2 Browse & open.” Round 4 client requested full implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming original-page opening task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker included “Tag persistence + suggestions” and note UI. Round 4 client explicitly requested implementation including tags and notes.
decisions.note: Conforming tag assignment and suggestion task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker included “Update/delete repo + API, refresh, duplicate→edit UI.” Round 4 client requested “editing, deletion, refresh” in the full implementation.
decisions.note: Conforming edit, delete, and duplicate-to-edit task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker included “Full search across all fields + tag filter.” Round 4 client requested full implementation including search and filtering.
decisions.note: Conforming search-corpus and tag-filter task decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 presented the task implementation as the approved plan's “Full search across all fields + tag filter,” with no task for #tag, Boolean/grouped, or exact-phrase parsing. Round 4 client requested “search, and filtering” but did not state any of those query-syntax expectations.
decisions.note: The task gate carried forward the simplified plan without the required advanced search grammar; the response did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reported saving as verified and auto-enrichment of title, description, favicon, and preview as best-effort and non-blocking. Round 5 client accepted the completed app.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented save and metadata behavior at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: “Tags & notes with tag-reuse suggestions — verified.” Round 5 client accepted the app.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented tag assignment and autocomplete behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reported “Browse newest-first, open in new tab.” Round 5 client said the completed app matched the approved behavior.
decisions.note: Opening a bookmark in a new tab is functionally conforming navigation to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reported “Edit, delete (with confirmation), refresh details” as verified. Round 5 client accepted the app.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented edit and delete behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reported “Duplicate → guides you to edit the existing one,” including trailing-slash variants. Round 5 client accepted the completed app.
decisions.note: Conforming implemented duplicate handling.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reported search across title, address, description, note, and tags plus a tag filter, and said everything except the equivalent SQLite-library substitution matched the approved plan. Round 5 client accepted it as matching the approved behavior.
decisions.note: The implemented field corpus, case-insensitive plan behavior, and tag filter conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker described implemented search only as field search “+ tag filter” and stated it matched the approved substring-search plan. Round 5 client said only that the completed app matched the approved behavior and accepted it.
decisions.note: The implementation review retained the plan's lack of #tag syntax, Boolean/grouped queries, and quoted exact phrases. The final approval did not express those expectations or identify their absence.
